title: Systemic Causes of Chronic Pruritus
subtitle: Cholestatic vs Uremic vs Hodgkin Lymphoma — distinguishing features

entities.name: Cholestatic Pruritus
entities.detail: Pruritus driven by impaired bile flow (PBC, PSC, drug-induced, ICP). Bile acids, endogenous opioids, and lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) all implicated as pruritogens.

entities.name: Uremic / CKD-Associated Pruritus
entities.detail: Affects 40-70% of hemodialysis patients. Multifactorial: uremic toxins, κ-opioid receptor dysregulation, small-fiber neuropathy, mast cell activation, and systemic inflammation.

entities.name: Hodgkin Lymphoma-Associated Pruritus
entities.detail: Cytokine-mediated systemic pruritus; occurs in 10-35% of classical Hodgkin lymphoma. A paraneoplastic phenomenon that may antedate the diagnosis by months to years.

values.cholestatic: Generalized; often starts palms and soles; worst at extremities; may involve entire body in severe disease. Mucous membranes and scalp typically spared.
values.uremic: Generalized; often symmetrically involves trunk and limbs; back (interscapular) is a common predilection site; face relatively spared; may be localized in mild disease.
values.hodgkin: Highly variable; often generalized; lower extremities and upper trunk reported more common; may be unilateral or bilateral; no consistent anatomic predilection.

values.cholestatic: Nocturnal predominance (worse at night); aggravated by heat and hot water; palmar-plantar itch classically worse at rest and at night — disrupts sleep significantly.
values.uremic: Fluctuating intensity; often worse after dialysis sessions or in late afternoon/evening; aggravated by heat, dry skin, and sweating; may improve transiently post-dialysis.
values.hodgkin: Often intense, burning, or stinging quality; may be triggered or worsened by alcohol ingestion (pathognomonic in subset); nocturnal pattern common but less consistent than cholestatic; can be paroxysmal and severe.

values.cholestatic: ↑ ALP (often >3× ULN), ↑ GGT, ↑ direct bilirubin (variable), ↑ serum bile acids (most sensitive); AMA+ in PBC (>95%); normal or mildly ↑ transaminases in pure cholestasis.
values.uremic: ↑ Serum creatinine (>3 mg/dL typically), ↑ BUN, hyperphosphatemia, ↓ GFR; anemia of CKD (normochromic normocytic); elevated PTH (secondary hyperparathyroidism); uremic toxins (beta-2 microglobulin, indoxyl sulfate).
values.hodgkin: ↑ ESR, ↑ LDH (prognostic marker), ↑ uric acid (high tumor burden), eosinophilia (variable), lymphopenia in advanced disease; elevated TARC (thymus and activation-regulated chemokine); IL-6 and IL-31 elevated; CBC may show anemia of chronic disease.

values.cholestatic: Bile acids accumulate in skin → activate Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor (MRGPRX4) on sensory neurons and release endogenous opioids. Lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) from autotaxin is a key pruritogen independent of bile acids. Endogenous opioid imbalance (↑ μ-opioid / ↓ κ-opioid tone).
values.uremic: Uremic toxins (β-2 microglobulin, indoxyl sulfate) → mast cell activation + IL-2 release. κ-Opioid receptor downregulation → imbalanced opioid signaling (↑ μ relative to κ). Small-fiber peripheral neuropathy with reduced IENFD. Secondary hyperparathyroidism → calcium-phosphate cutaneous deposition.
values.hodgkin: Malignant Reed-Sternberg cells release cytokines: IL-31 (major pruritogen — activates IL-31RA on sensory neurons), IL-6, IL-13, thymus and activation-regulated chemokine (TARC/CCL17). Pruritus is a paraneoplastic manifestation of type 2 immune skewing by tumor microenvironment.

values.cholestatic: RUQ abdominal ultrasound first (bile duct dilation, gallstones, hepatic parenchyma, splenomegaly); MRCP if PSC suspected (biliary strictures); liver biopsy if AMA− and diagnosis uncertain.
values.uremic: Imaging not required for diagnosis; renal ultrasound to assess CKD chronicity (small echogenic kidneys) and exclude obstructive uropathy if acute CKD; no specific imaging for pruritus evaluation in established CKD.
values.hodgkin: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis (staging); PET-CT preferred (FDG-avid disease — Deauville criteria for response assessment); CXR as rapid screen for mediastinal widening; excisional lymph node biopsy for histologic diagnosis.

values.cholestatic: Cholestyramine 4g QID (bile acid sequestrant); if ineffective after 2 weeks → rifampin 150mg BID (PXR agonist enhancing bile acid clearance). Naltrexone 50mg QD (μ-opioid antagonist) for refractory. Sertraline as alternative. Treat underlying liver disease (UDCA for PBC, stop offending drug).
values.uremic: Optimize dialysis adequacy (Kt/V ≥1.2); gabapentin 100-300mg post-dialysis (α-2-δ calcium channel modulator); difelikefalin 0.5 mcg/kg IV post-dialysis (FDA-approved 2021, κ-opioid agonist). Emollients for barrier restoration. Nalfurafine where available (Japan/Korea).
values.hodgkin: Chemotherapy is definitive (ABVD or BV-AVD → pruritus resolves with tumor response). Bridge therapy while awaiting treatment: antihistamines, mirtazapine 15-30mg QHS, gabapentin 300mg TID, aprepitant (NK1R antagonist) for paraneoplastic itch. Pruritus is an indirect prognostic marker.

values.cholestatic: Pruritus improves with disease control (UDCA in PBC slows progression but does not reliably relieve itch). In ICP: delivery at 36-37 weeks is curative — itch resolves within days postpartum. In drug-induced cholestasis: resolution within weeks of drug withdrawal. End-stage liver disease: transplant is definitive.
values.uremic: Pruritus persists as long as CKD/ESRD is present; improves with increased dialysis dose but rarely resolves completely on dialysis. Kidney transplantation is the most effective treatment — pruritus resolves in most patients within weeks of transplant as GFR recovers.
values.hodgkin: Pruritus resolves completely in the majority of patients achieving complete remission with chemotherapy. Recurrence of pruritus after remission should prompt evaluation for relapsed disease. In rare cases, pruritus persists post-treatment, suggesting paraneoplastic sensitization or coexistent chronic pruritus etiology.

values.cholestatic: Palmar-plantar itch + nocturnal predominance in a middle-aged woman → always check ALP and AMA (PBC). Pruritus in third trimester pregnancy + elevated bile acids → ICP; fetal risk is real — do not delay delivery beyond 37 weeks. PMID 29385376.
values.uremic: Pruritus in CKD patients is frequently underdiagnosed and undertreated. Severity does not correlate reliably with BUN/creatinine levels — screen for pruritus in every CKD/dialysis patient visit using Worst Itching Intensity NRS. Difelikefalin is the only FDA-approved drug specifically for CKD-associated pruritus. PMID 29385376.
values.hodgkin: ★ RED FLAG: Intense, burning, generalized pruritus — especially if severe enough to disrupt sleep or if worsened by alcohol — in a young adult with lymphadenopathy is Hodgkin lymphoma until proven otherwise. Pruritus may precede lymphoma diagnosis by 6 months to 5 years. Never attribute undiagnosed chronic pruritus to psychosomatic causes without a full hematologic workup. PMID 29385376.
